events.continuity_hook: Moves the St. Pete family trip from the revised package comparison into booking decisions before the better cancellable room disappears.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flight, Gulf-side hotel, rental car, and seat plan, while identifying the remaining hotel fee and room-category details Maya should verify before purchase.
events.scenario_brief: Maya and her spouse decide that staying Gulf-side is worth more than the larger inland suite for the short Thursday, August 6 to Sunday, August 9 beach trip. The cancellable family room near the beach is close to selling out, and the Thursday morning ATL-to-TPA nonstop plus late-afternoon Sunday return still price better than Sarasota. Maya wants to move from comparison to booking for three travelers, decide whether to add a midsize rental car, and choose seats that keep the child between or next to both adults. The hotel still has paid breakfast, resort and parking fees, and an unresolved balcony upcharge.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip pass for the St. Pete family beach weekend after bookings are set and weather becomes the main variable.
events.interaction_goal: Create a practical two-day-out checklist and flag the few items Maya should recheck before leaving for the airport.
events.scenario_brief: The St. Pete flights, Gulf-side hotel, and rental car are booked, and departure is only a couple of days away. The airline posts a minor return-time adjustment that still gets the family home before bedtime, while the forecast now shows afternoon thunderstorms and possible beach-flag restrictions. The hotel confirms the pool, paid parking, and luggage storage, but early room readiness is not guaranteed. Maya wants a compact family departure plan covering ATL timing, TPA arrival, tolls and parking, a grocery stop, first-night dinner, breakfast alternatives, rainy-window activities, pool timing, and whether any better adjacent or window seats have opened.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new solo work-travel episode after the August family trip wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Minneapolis work trip, identify viable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details Maya needs before routing a plan for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After the Florida weekend, Maya is assigned to a Minneapolis client training and workflow-mapping visit planned for Monday, September 14 through Thursday, September 17. The client may use either a downtown training center or a hospital-campus room near the university area, and it is not yet clear whether Monday requires an in-person welcome meeting or can stay remote. Maya wants ATL-to-MSP flights that avoid an unnecessarily early start, a Thursday return that does not create a rushed exit, and a well-reviewed hotel with simple mornings and dinner options nearby. The unresolved pieces are the exact site, first required in-person time, Thursday end time, and whether downtown transit and rideshares are enough or a rental car is needed.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Minneapolis planning after the client confirms the downtown site and most of the meeting schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight, hotel, and ground-transport combinations and choose the package Maya should send for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the main sessions will be at the downtown training center, with Tuesday and Wednesday running 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and a Thursday closeout from 10:00 a.m. to noon. Monday prep can be handled remotely unless a late-afternoon welcome is added. Flight options include a Monday midday Delta nonstop into MSP, a cheaper one-stop itinerary arriving during the evening rush, and an after-work nonstop that would make the first night tight. Thursday choices include a midafternoon nonstop with little cushion and an early-evening nonstop that fits the closeout better. Hotels include a skyway-connected downtown property with strong reviews and on-site dining but paid breakfast, a nearby limited-service hotel with included breakfast but a longer walk, and an airport-area hotel with an easier rate but a poor morning commute.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Minneapolis episode from approval into booking after the Monday welcome meeting makes the midday outbound the clear choice.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flight timing, hotel booking details, seat selections, and no-rental-car plan before the fare hold expires.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Monday midday nonstop, the early-evening Thursday return, and the skyway-connected downtown hotel as long as the rate remains cancellable. The client then adds a Monday 5:00 p.m. welcome walk-through and a Wednesday group dinner near the training center, making the after-work outbound a poor fit and reducing the need for a rental car. The fare hold expires that night, the hotel can note a quiet room away from elevators, and breakfast is still paid unless she uses nearby cafes. Seat maps show a few window seats toward the back and more forward aisle seats.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for Minneapolis after flights, hotel, meeting times, and downtown logistics are mostly settled.
events.interaction_goal: Build a concise Minneapolis travel checklist and identify the small set of details Maya should recheck the day before flying.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before departure, Maya has the ATL-to-MSP nonstop, downtown hotel, and early-evening Thursday return booked. The client confirms badge pickup at 7:45 a.m. Tuesday and says the Thursday closeout should end by 11:30 a.m. A rainy forecast and downtown roadwork could affect airport transfers, and the hotel reports a temporary closure on one skyway segment. Breakfast remains paid at the hotel, but there are early cafes nearby. Maya wants a final logistics pass covering ATL timing, MSP-to-hotel transportation, luggage storage, Tuesday walking route, breakfast workarounds, dinner after arrival, receipts, Thursday airport timing, and whether any better window seats have opened.
